html:
Uncle Boonmee Who Can Recall His Past Lives is a 2010 film by the Thai director Apichatpong Weerasethakul. It won the Palme d'Or at the Cannes Film Festival, the first film from Southeast Asia to do so.

Boonmee is a farmer dying of kidney failure in the countryside of Isan, northeastern Thailand. In his last days the ghost of his dead wife comes to dinner, and his lost son returns as a hairy creature with red eyes. He walks into a cave where he thinks he was born in an earlier life. The film moves slowly, mixes ghosts and animals with daily life, and takes rebirth as a plain fact, as many people in rural Thailand do.

It was part of a larger art project about the Isan town of Nabua, where the army fought communist rebels in the 1960s and 1970s, and it quietly touches on that violence. The prize brought world attention to Thai art cinema.
sum: Uncle Boonmee Who Can Recall His Past Lives is a 2010 film by the Thai director Apichatpong Weerasethakul. It won the Palme d'Or at the Cannes Film Festival, the first film from Southeast Asia to do so.
